handDesc.handNote: Main text and any darker interventions are distinguished where observed. No individual historical correcting hands are inferred from tonal contrast in monochrome photographs.

origin.p: The supplied BnF IIIF manifest dates the manuscript to 1001–1100. The catalogue dating is not a date assigned to individual interventions.

surrogates.p: The original full-resolution digital images and enlarged crops were inspected for this first pass. Gallica source reuse conditions apply. No text was populated from LL or another witness.

projectDesc.p: Source-grounded first reading of all 48 annotated verse positions, with manuscript-specific spellings and observed interventions. A different agent subsequently inspected all source verses and every evidence note; see revision record and second-pass ledger.

correction.p: No silent emendation from an edition or another witness. Local uncertain letters use unclear, irrecoverable text or signs use gap. Observed above-line letters use add. Tonal distinctions use hi without an invented underlying erased text or historical hand. Manuscript annotations use note type manuscript, distinct from editorial evidence notes.

normalization.p: One source-oriented display. Ordinary allographs, long s, and capitals are represented in legible Latin types. Word boundaries are editorially segmented; no indentation whitespace is inserted inside verse mixed content. Selected ligatures and abbreviation signs are declared typographic approximations; explicit expansions remain in TEI rather than a separate reading mode. This is not a facsimile-perfect inventory of every minute stroke.

punctuation.p: Significant observed punctuation is retained schematically, without adding systematic modern sentence punctuation.

segmentation.p: Each l represents a verse and physical written line at its canonical poem position. Elegiac couplets and even-line indentation are editorial display grouping. Page breaks follow the photographed left/right physical pages. Facsimile zones reproduce the existing annotation rectangles unchanged; they may include neighbouring ink and exclude marginal annotations.

interpretation.p: First-pass evidence notes are a working queue for an independent agent, not assignments for the human editor. Genuine source uncertainty remains local; consequential unresolved interpretation is distinguished from ordinary observation.

revisionDesc.change: Independent second-agent source review of all 48 verses and every editorial note. Corrected first-pass Formonsas to source Formonsa at31. Retained the short uncertain reading at33, qualified contraction at23, and other faint source text without editorial supplementation. No human approval is implied.
Completed first reading from source images and enlarged crops, with line coverage and evidence notes. Independent second reading not yet performed.

AD PERIURĀ
AMICEEsse deos i crede fidem iurata fefellit
&et facies illi quae fuit ante manet
Quam longos habuit nondum periura capillos
Tam longos postquam numina laesit hab&et
Candida candorem roseo suffusa colore
Ante fuit niueo luc&et in ore rubor
Pes erat exiguus pedis est aptissima forma
Longa decensque fuit longa decensque manet
Argutos habuit radiant ut sidus ocelli
Per quos mentita est perfida saepe mihi
Scilicet aeterno falsum iurare puellis
Di quoque concedunt formaque numen hab&et
Perque suos illam nuper iurasse recordor
Perque meos oculos &et doluere mei
Dicite di si uos impune fefellerat illa
Alterius meriti cur ego damna tuli
An non inuidiae uobis cepheia uirgo est
Pro male formonsa iussa parente mori
Non satis est quod uos habui sine pondere testes
Et mecum lusos ridet inulta deos
Ut sua per nostrum redimat periuria poenam
Victima deceptus decipientis ero
Aut sine re nomen d̄sdeus est frustraque timetur
Et stulta populos credulitate mouet
Aut si quis deus est teneras amat ille puellas
Et nimium solas omnia posse iubet
Nobis fatifero mauors accingitur ensi
Nos petit inuicta palladis asta manu
Nobis flexibiles curuantur apollinis arcus
In nos alta iouis dextera fulmen hab&et
Formonsa superi metuunt offendere laesi
Atque ultro quae se non timuere timent
Et quisquam pia tura imponere curat
Certe plus animi deb&et inesse uiris
Iuppiter igne suo lucos iaculatur &et arces
Missaque periuris tela ferire uetat
Tot meruere peti semele miserabilis arsit
Officio est illi poena reperta suo
At si uenturo se subduxiss&et amanti
Non pater in baccho matris haber&et opus
Quid queror &et toto facio conuicia caelo
Di quoque habent oculos di quoque pectus habent
Si deus ipse forem numen sine fraude licer&et
Femina mendaci fallere uoce meum
Ipse ego iurarem uerum iurare puellas
Et non de tetricis dicerer esse deis
Tu tamen illorum moderatius utere dono
Aut oculis certe parce puella meis

div.head: Independently reviewed source notes
div.note: The large initial E spans the first two verses. A separate right-margin title reads AD followed by a faint marked word, tentatively PERIURĀ, then AMICE on the next line. The uncertain middle word and its mark are recorded without silently asserting a full expansion or historical hand.

A terminal et ligature occurs in habet and similarly in several later verbal endings. The selected signs are represented schematically as g within abbr/expan rather than expanded silently. Ordinary word-internal allographs remain typographic approximations.
The visible sequence is aeterno; it is retained without grammatical or cross-witness regularization.
The visible word is represented meriti. Its darker first letters are not a warrant to invent an erased underlying reading or a distinct historical hand.
The source spelling formonsa is retained, as is formonsa at31 after the independent reading. The name cepheia at17 follows the source letter sequence.
The sequence Ut sua per nostrum redimat periuria poenam follows the image, without changing nostrum or other forms to fit an expected syntax.
The short marked form between nomen and est is represented tentatively as d̄s, with a low-certainty expansion deus. The small contraction mark is not fully clear in this photograph.
The final word ensi is faded and retained locally in unclear. It is not completed from a normalized text.
The word before manu is visibly asta; no initial h has been silently supplied.

The final word laesi is faint. The adjacent final line32 has a faded middle sequence read non timuere. Both remain local source uncertainties after the independent reading. The opening formonsa has no separately visible final s before superi.

The photograph provides a short faded sequence read pia tura between quisquam and imponere. No additional word has been supplied in this interval. The following line34 also has a faint animi, retained locally as unclear.

The first half of45 is markedly faded; Ipse ego iurarem is retained as a tentative reading. At46 the short sequence following Et is tentatively non de. Both uncertainties describe source legibility, not a human assignment to choose another edition.
